title: Compact invocation profiles and SDK tiling (PRD draft)
summary: Draft PRD exploring a compact, typed invocation profile model for the Hosted API that reduces handshake overhead for streaming + tool-calling flows and a complementary SDK tiling pattern for low-latency clients. Focus: make partial/resumable streams cheaper and easier to integrate while preserving structured output and tool safety.
problem_statement: Current streaming handshakes and tool-calling contracts in the Hosted API are heavy for low-bandwidth clients and mobile embedding. Each tool call often requires a full session negotiation, and SDKs end up copying orchestration logic (retry, resume, schema reconciliation). Result: high p99 latency, duplicated client logic, and brittle partial-response handling.
proposed_solution: Introduce a compact invocation profile (CIP) layer: a small, typed descriptor attached to requests that encodes expected streaming behavior, acceptable partial outputs, and tool-call affordances. Complement CIP with an SDK tiling pattern (lightweight client primitives + a small runtime) that handles resume, local validation of structured frames, and backpressure policies.
product_requirements: CIP descriptor schema (<= 512 bytes) that can be sent as a header or first frame
SDK: 'tile' primitive that exposes onChunk/onToolCall/onComplete and built-in resume/reconciliation code
Server: fast-path for CIP-enabled requests with reduced protocol round-trips
Tool calling: compact tool handshake that can piggyback on CIP when tool contracts are simple
Structured output: declarative frame types with versioned schema pointers (human readable IDs)
Observability: token-level and frame-level telemetry surfaced in Console for CIP flows
Compatibility: fall back to existing streaming protocol when CIP is absent
SLA: CIP fast-path must reduce median first-byte latency by at least 15% on targeted mobile profiles
api_sketch: User-visible surface: extend existing /v1/generate endpoint to accept header 'X-Invocation-Profile' with base64-encoded CIP. CIP fields: profile_id, expected_frames (list of short symbols), resume_strategy (none|kv-cache|session-snapshot), tool_affordance (none|stateless|stateful-id), client_hint (low-bandwidth|interactive|batch). Server fast-path: if CIP.profile_id in curated fast-path list, accept the request and open an optimized stream connection. Example CIP (pseudo): {profile_id: 'compact-interactive-v1', expected_frames: ['text','action'], resume_strategy:'kv-cache', tool_affordance:'stateless', client_hint:'interactive'}. Note: CIP decodes to <=512 bytes.
sdk_ergonomics_notes: Goal: SDKs should ship a 'tiling runtime' ~10–30KB that developers instantiate per route. Minimal API: tile = createTile({profile: CIP, handlers: {onChunk, onAction, onMeta}}); tile.start(input); tile.resume(snapshot). The runtime handles: deduping frame fragments, reconciling partial JSON frames, automatic bounded retries (with exponential backoff and client-side idempotency tokens), and local schema validation against bundled small schemas. Edge cases: provide both promise and callback patterns (for node/browser/native). Keep default surface minimal; advanced customization via opts.
streaming_resume_behavior: We propose two resume modes supported by CIP: 1) kv-cache resume: server retains small KV-session state keyed by resume_token for short TTL (e.g., 60s). Client supplies resume_token; server replays latest frame cursor. 2) snapshot resume: client supplies last stable snapshot (opaque), server merges if compatible. For low-bandwidth clients the SDK should compress resume metadata; for sensitive workloads resume_token must be bound to the auth context. IMPORTANT: resume only for partial-safe routes (marked in CIP), otherwise server rejects resume attempts.
tool_call_handshake: Compact tool handshake: a lightweight initial tool descriptor can be included in CIP when tool shape is simple (name, idempotency, minimal schema id). For complex tool calls use the existing long-form tool call flow. The compact handshake supports speculative tooling: server may send a 'tool-ready' frame early, allowing SDK to prefetch credentials or cold-start local adapters. Handshake flow (compact): 1) client indicates tool_affordance:stateless and includes tool hint; 2) server responds with tool-token frame (if needed) then streams tool invocation result as 'action' frames. Safety: for any tool-afforded CIP, server enforces a strict allowlist and records a linked_artifact in telemetry.
structured_output_strategy: Use small, composable frame types (text, json-frame, action, meta) where json-frame has schema_id and a compact delta format for incremental updates. Adopt a scheme where schema_id maps to a tiny human-friendly ID (e.g., 'rdw/summ-v2') that resolves to a schema in our hosted schema registry (Console). SDKs should bundle frequently-used schemas to avoid runtime fetches; fallback to on-demand fetch with caching. For partial JSON, prefer patch-style diffs (RFC-like) limited to core fields to keep framing small. Encourage canonicalization rules to reduce client-side reconciliation complexity.
observability_and_migrations: Instrument: frame type counts, resume attempts, tool-affordance usage, CIP decode errors
Console: per-route CIP adoption dashboard and resume success rate
Migration: opt-in flag for customers to enable CIP fast-path for a subset of routes
Migration: provide server-side compatibility shim that accepts CIP but does not enable fast-path until opted-in
Rollout plan: internal alpha with mobile partners -> wider beta -> GA after telemetry targets
open_questions: TTL and billing model for kv-cache resume: bill for retained state or include as infra cost?
Security binding for resume_token across private deployments (VPC/on-prem): require HMAC vs. encrypted token?
Schema registry sync model for Private deployments: replicate schemas or require local registry?
What should be the default CIP size limit (we propose 512 bytes) and how do we validate/negotiation failures?
Should we expose a high-level 'tiling runtime' across languages or language-specific idiomatic SDKs?
